text: Git branching is a powerful tool for managing your code. Instead of working directly on the main version, you create a feature branch. This is a separate copy where you can develop new features or fix bugs without affecting the stable code. Once your work is complete, you merge that branch back into the main branch. However, before merging, you typically submit a pull request. This allows your teammates to review your changes, suggest improvements, and discuss potential problems. This workflow, part of version control, keeps your project organized, prevents conflicts, and ensures that the main branch always remains reliable. It’s a standard practice for both solo developers and large teams.
